claims.text: Gradient nanostructuring of a metallic alloy can concurrently improve strength and ductility.
Surface mechanical attrition treatment can produce a nanostructured surface layer.
The surface nanostructure produced by gradient processing can transition gradually into the coarse-grained bulk.
The proposed gradient microstructure consists of a nanograined surface layer and an interior retaining the original coarse-grained structure.
The nanostructured surface layer enhances strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
A gradual transition from the nanostructured surface to the coarse-grained interior mitigates stress concentrations.
The gradient microstructure delays crack propagation.
Mitigation of stress concentrations and delayed crack propagation preserve ductility.
Gradient processing is predicted to increase yield strength relative to the untreated material.
Gradient processing is predicted to improve strain-to-failure relative to the untreated material.
The efficacy of gradient nanostructuring may depend on processing parameters and alloy composition.
Extreme strain rates or temperatures may negate the beneficial effects of the gradient microstructure.
